beats.beat: A B Infrabuild operates in two segments: creation of infrastructure and operating a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant. It builds railways (platforms, station buildings, gauge conversion, track laying), bridges (various types including beam, cantilever, arch, suspension, cable-stayed and truss bridges), and roads (bituminous and concrete). Its RMC plant at Kashimira, Thane, is a state-of-the-art facility.

Contracts are won through a competitive tender process: clients issue tenders, pre-bid meetings are held, the lowest bidder is awarded the contract and must deposit a performance guarantee before execution.

The company’s major customers include government bodies such as Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM), Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Ltd (MRVCL), Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd, and several private entities. Western Railway alone contributed 52% of the orders on hand. For the year ended March 31, 2018, the top customers accounted for 57% of total revenue.

The order book is concentrated in Mumbai and Maharashtra, and the company uses a 'box pushing' technique for executing projects. It claims healthy order book, experienced management with over 20 years in the infrastructure industry, and investment in advanced machinery.
Key dependencies identified in the SWOT analysis include slow pace of government projects, working capital crunch that may affect profitability, and changes in government policies.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has declined over the five reported years: from ₹8,661.35 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹6,053.05 lakhs in FY2018, with peaks at ₹9,021.12 lakhs in FY2015 and ₹7,452.76 in FY2016. The drop is most pronounced from FY2015 to FY2016 and again from FY2017 to FY2018.

Net profit after adjustments has been volatile: ₹95.95 lakhs in FY2014, ₹78.36 lakhs in FY2015, ₹32.63 lakhs in FY2016, then a sharp dip to ₹15.86 lakhs in FY2017 followed by a recovery to ₹314.66 lakhs in FY2018. The FY2018 figure is the highest in the five-year period.
Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax (EBITDA) stood at ₹784.46 lakhs in FY2014, ₹945.78 lakhs in FY2015, ₹783.31 lakhs in FY2016, ₹676.19 lakhs in FY2017, and ₹928.80 lakhs in FY2018.

The company carries substantial debt. Long-term borrowings decreased from ₹586.63 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹133.09 lakhs in FY2018, but short-term borrowings increased from ₹3,082.27 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹3,537.35 lakhs in FY2018. Total borrowings (long+short) remained above ₹3,600 lakhs throughout the period.

The filing discloses that the company had negative cash flows in recent financial years, which could adversely impact business. Failure to recover trade receivables on time is also highlighted as a risk.

beats.beat: The sole promoter of the company is Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 74,95,476 equity shares, representing 90.949% of the pre-issue equity share capital.

Other directors hold only 300 shares each: Bharat Kumar Parmar, Shree Prakash Singh, and Mukesh Pandey (all Whole Time Directors). Key management personnel include Ms. Anchal Pachori (CFO, age 28, CA) and Mr. Mohit Soni (Company Secretary, age 26, ACS). Mr. Hatim Sakerwala holds 9% of equity shares.

Related party transactions: Loans taken from KMP/Board of Directors amounted to ₹68.4 lakhs in FY2018. Director remuneration paid was ₹57.7 lakhs. Outstanding payables to related parties as on March 31, 2018 were ₹324.3 lakhs.

Red flags: The promoter’s two companies – Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited – were struck off by the Registrar of Companies in March 2016 due to non-operation of business. The company has issued equity shares in the last 12 months at a price that may be lower than the issue price. No independent appraisal agency has been appointed for the project, and no monitoring agency for fund deployment.
No criminal cases or investigations against directors, and none of the directors appear on the RBI list of willful defaulters.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild operates in the infrastructure and construction sector, which contributes about 8% to India’s GDP (at constant prices). The market is highly fragmented and working capital intensive.

India’s construction market was valued at US$400 billion in 2015 and is expected to reach US$1,000 billion by 2025. The logistics sector is projected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% from US$160 billion in 2017 to US$215 billion by 2020. India’s GDP growth has been above 7% and the eight core industries grew 4.2% in 2017-18.

Key growth drivers include government flagship programs (Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India, Power for All), eased FDI norms in 15 sectors including real estate and construction, rising industrialization and urbanization, and an expected increase in working age population to 64% by 2021. India requires US$ 777.73 billion in infrastructure investment by 2022.
Headwinds acknowledged by the company include the slow pace of government projects, a working capital crunch that may affect profitability, and changes in government policies.
Competition comes from both organized and unorganized players. The sector is highly fragmented, and the company does not name specific competitors in the filing.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is an infrastructure and construction company based in Mumbai, working on railways, bridges, roads and operating a ready-mix concrete plant. It is proposing a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares to list on the SME board.
The company has been in business for over a decade, counting Western Railway, Central Railway and MCGM among its major clients.
Proceeds from the issue will be used primarily to meet working capital requirements of ₹1,130 lakhs, with the remainder for general corporate purposes.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of face value ₹10 each at a price to be determined. There is no offer for sale component.
The lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited, and the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.

Proceeds from the fresh issue will be used: (1) to meet working capital requirements of ₹1,130 lakhs, and (2) for general corporate purposes (amount not disclosed). The company has not appointed an independent agency for appraisal of the project, nor a monitoring agency for fund deployment.

beats.beat: Dependence on Indian Railways: In Fiscal 2018, Indian Railways contributed 57% of the company’s revenue. Losing this customer would cause a significant revenue dip.
Negative cash flows: The company has experienced negative cash flows in recent financial years. Sustained negative cash flow could impair business and financial condition.
Unsecured loans repayable on demand: As of March 31, 2018, the company had ₹405.02 lakhs in unsecured loans that are repayable on demand. A call from lenders could strain cash flow.
Promoter’s struck-off companies: Two companies promoted by Amit Mishra were struck off by the ROC for non-operation. This may reflect on promoter track record.
Related party transactions: The company has entered into related party transactions in the past and may continue to do so, potentially not on arm’s length terms.

beats.beat: The filing includes a 'Basis for Issue Price' section that provides EPS, RoNW and other ratios for the company. For FY2018, the company reports an EPS of ₹28.14 (likely based on post-issue capital?) and RoNW of 44.71%. For FY2017, EPS was ₹1.97 and RoNW 12.39%. However, the filing does not name any peer companies for comparison. The peer comparison table in the DRHP appears to include only the company’s own ratios, without listing external peers.
Without named peers, it is not possible to construct a peer-based valuation range. The issue price will be determined by the company in consultation with the lead manager, as stated in the filing.
